newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - April 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Draft budget for 1997/98 fiscal year to be presented before parliament in May. The draft will try to satisfy the economic operators and politicians as well prior to general elections in the second half of the year.
- Some agricultural areas received plenty of rain during April compared with the same period in 1996.
- U.N. envoy for Western Sahara James Baker on a North Africa tour to try 'an American solution' to the dispute over the territory.
- Dispute between members of the opposition Koutla group (Democratic bloc) continues.
- Urban unemployment drops to 18 percent in 1996 from 23 percent in 1995. Half of Morocco's 10-million workforce is concentrated in cities.

- Morocco to launch a reform of its heavy administration. Story refers to World Bank recommendations aimed at modernising the public administration and dramatically reducing the number of civil servants.
- The public Treasury to face financing costs to cover its increasing deficit in future.

- Moroccan government to end soon the examination of 1997/98 draft budget. The budget will suffer from the weight of foreign and domestic debt and extra-spending. The domestic debt is estimated at 122 billion dirhams ($13 billion) and foreign debt at $21 billion.
- Leading Banque Commerciale du Maroc holds a seminar on upgrading the Moroccan private sector enterprises which will face the 21st century's tough competition.

- The Casablanca stock exchange is on declining trend. Story refers to the bourse index which surged to 54 percent performance in the first four months of the year compared with the same period in 1996. The index is expected to slightly drop and stabilise in the coming weeks.
